item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon State’s loss at Fresno State
item.description: FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children’s Stadium. Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State. 1. Reality check Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching. The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn’t diminish what’s being accomplished this season. They’re simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now. 2. Oregon State was outcoached JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season. Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State’s tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter. 3. Self-inflicted errors can’t happen in games like this Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle’s would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton’s foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn’t occur. That doesn’t even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits. 4. The offensive line may have had its worst game Houston was more physically dominating than Fresno State, but that’s to be expected. Oregon State’s offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU’s rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it’s not a particularly stout group. 5. Josiah Freeman was the best receiver on the field Fresno State’s 6-foot-4 receiver had a big night with two touchdowns. Freeman had a massive advantage against Isaiah Houi and performed accordingly. If there’s one piece OSU’s receiving corps is missing it is a target with the size and length of Freeman, which the Beavers are leaning on via their tight ends. But an outside target like him is hard to beat and he showed why. 6. item.title: “Every player does their bit” Alan Shearer hails Arsenal’s defensive play
item.description: “Every player does their bit” Alan Shearer hails Arsenal’s defensive play Alan Shearer has praised Arsenal for the quality of their defensive performances, highlighting the collective effort that has helped the Gunners establish themselves as one of the strongest teams in the country. The former striker believes Mikel Arteta has built a side that understands the importance of defending together and protecting its goal. Arteta has gradually transformed the culture at Arsenal since taking charge, giving the club a clearer identity and building a team capable of competing for major honours. One of the biggest changes has been the way the Gunners approach matches, particularly their willingness to prioritise defensive organisation. Early in his time at the Emirates, Arteta wanted his players to produce attractive football, but the team sometimes sacrificed defensive stability in the process. That often left Arsenal vulnerable and resulted in goals being conceded too easily. The manager has since worked to correct those weaknesses, turning the Gunners into a difficult side to break down. Their defensive approach has attracted criticism from some rivals, but Arsenal have continued to show that organisation and discipline can be just as important as attacking brilliance. Shearer praises Arsenal’s collective defending Shearer has been particularly impressed by the way every Arsenal player contributes when the team is defending. The Gunners delivered another impressive defensive performance at the weekend , prompting the former England international to highlight their commitment and organisation. Speaking via the Metro , Shearer explained why he believes Arsenal’s approach makes them so difficult to play against. ‘That is how you work as a team, that is how you defend as a team. ‘Every single one of them to a man were outstanding. When they were under the cosh in the second half, you could see how much they wanted to defend and what it means to them to keep a clean sheet. ‘I don’t think there is a better team in world football that defend quite like Arsenal defend. Every player does their bit, it isn’t just the back four.’ (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Arteta has built a difficult team to beat Although the Gunners are sometimes criticised for placing so much emphasis on defending, their approach has helped them become more consistent. item.title: Pocognoli focus on Scotland tidy-up as Euros loom
item.description: When Sebastien Pocognoli's disjointed Scotland trudged off at a two-thirds-full Hampden after being well beaten by Slovenia, the intrigue that came with the start of the new boss' extended maiden camp had turned to a sense of deflation. A dominant display in a Nations League draw away to the Slovenians 10 days prior, plus another in a 2-0 victory at North Macedonia, had built optimism. A 3-0 defeat at home to Switzerland was written off after Jack Hendry's early red card was quickly followed by an opening goal for the 12th-ranked Fifa nation. A second straight Hampden loss under the Belgian felt different, though. Pocognoli's side were "outfought" and simply "not good enough", said captain Andy Robertson. Cut open defensively throughout by Slovenia, placed nine spots below Scotland in the world rankings, a sobering second-half showing led to questions about approach, systems and squad make-up. However, heading into a double-header against North Macedonia and Switzerland this month, which will conclude the Scots' Nations League campaign, Pocognoli insists this is more of a clean-up job rather than one that requires any radical change. "We want to continue what we produced in the first camp," the 39-year-old said after naming his latest squad , which marks the returns of Scott McTominay, Che Adams and Kieran Tierney, while James Penrice has received a first call-up as reward for an impressive run of form with Rangers. "There's no reason to change everything because I was happy with the camp. The main word is continuity [after the first camp]. "It's important to get some good results for sure. I was clear we need to find the right balance between changing things, experimenting and also being successful." McTominay returns as Penrice earns first Scotland call Honeymoon over as Pocognoli's Scotland suffer domestic disharmony Pocognoli seeks mood-shifting result In football's savage, reactive world, a deserved defeat at home to a team ranked outside the world's top 50 is bound to attract scrutiny. Given it was the final match of a four-game run before a six-week wait to attempt to put things right, that criticism only becomes prolonged. Pocognoli shared the Tartan Army's disappointment, but after a few days the "real feeling" came after a debut camp packed with new faces and "strong decisions". "When the disappointment was gone, the first feeling was positive," he said. "We did a lot of good things. "But we need a good result to give something to the supporters and give confidence to the players that we are winning games - that's the main factor in qualifying for tournaments. "We want to just continue the good things we showed in Slovenia and North Macedonia in a very short period of time, to keep the fragment of these games and to try to clean some situations." [BBC] The 'big job' coming up Despite the positivity Pocognoli is harbouring, he is not oblivious to the fact Scotland need to improve this month. His side are third in Nations League Group B1

item.title: Andoni Iraola gives Ryan Gravenberch injury update after Liverpool star misses Fenerbahce trip
item.description: Andoni Iraola has not ruled out a possible return for Ryan Gravenberch this weekend after it was confirmed the Dutchman will play no part in the club’s Champions League trip to Fenerbahce through injury. Liverpool midfielder Gravenberch was absent from the 22-man travelling squad that flew out to Turkey on Tuesday morning, left behind on Merseyside to have treatment on a heel issue. Iraola provided an update on the 24-year-old’s status at a press conference at Fenerbahce’s Chobani Stadium, which was delayed by over an hour due to traffic issues in Istanbul. Asked if Gravenberch could be available again for this Sunday’s trip to Crystal Palace, he said: “I don’t know, it’s a day-to-day thing. It’s the heel, it’s about the pain. Ryan Gravenberch is sidelined for Liverpool's trip to Fenerbahce with a heel problem (Getty) “I think he’s been in some discomfort. The other day against Arsenal, he was warming up and he was not fully confident. He hasn't improved since then, but it's going be something that every day we ask him, every day we see how he is. “If he can be available for the weekend, lovely. It would be a very good help for us, but I cannot tell you right now.” The Netherlands international was an unused substitute in Sunday’s defeat to Arsenal , with Trey Nyoni preferred in midfield as the 19-year-old made his first Premier League start. Gravenberch’s absence likely opens up another opportunity for Nyoni in the starting XI against Fenerbahce. Trey Nyoni made his first Premier League start on the weekend after being preferred to Gravenberch (Getty) “ I think he has to continue in the same place that has been since the beginning of pre-season, being ready for every game,” Iraola added. “I think he's playing most of the games or even all the games lately, so we trust him. “He's doing very well and I think we have to encourage him to continue improving, continue learning, continue adding experience. But he's in a very good place.” Iraola was left furious after the Arsenal result after a penalty appeal surrounding a shirt-pull on Alexander Isak was waved away by referee Andy Madley and VAR, asserting after the game that he will tell his players to dive in order to get officials to take appropriate action. Despite his anger, Iraola confirmed that he had not asked refereeing body Pro Ref for a formal explanation why the penalty wasn’t awarded. “No, I didn’t ask for an explanation,” he said. “I told you what I think about the plays, but honestly I don’t have time. “Preparing for Fenerbahce, we have just two days between games, so I’ve just been focussing on this game, the opposition and how to prepare the team for tomorrow.”

item.title: Insider Reveals Red Sox Will Continue To Pursue Trade For This NL All-Star
item.description: Boston Red Sox chief baseball officer Craig Breslow The Boston Red Sox have Trevor Story at shortstop and Franklin Arias ready to take over when they move on from Story. However, there were reports at the trade deadline that they were aggressively pursuing a trade for an established star shortstop. They were linked to Otto Lopez, Jeremy Peña, Elly De La Cruz and CJ Abrams. Their position on adding a shortstop does not seem to have changed. According to The Athletic's Jim Bowden , the team will be looking to improve the offense at multiple positions. "The Red Sox will also continue to call the (Washington) Nationals regarding a possible CJ Abrams trade," Bowden wrote on Tuesday. Abrams is one of the best young players in baseball, and trading for him would require a haul that would have to include Arias. Abrams is under contract through 2028 and is already a two-time All-Star. In the last three years, he has a .777 OPS and 72 home runs. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? As much as the Nationals would like to keep him and James Wood, they likely know that they are not close to competing with them and could trade both of them for a return that sets them up for the future. Abrams would be a great addition to any lineup. He is a terrible defender at shortstop, so the Red Sox may not want to keep him there. However, they have no shortage of capable defenders on the team. Abrams could move to second base, where he saw some time at the end of the year, and the Red Sox could move Caleb Durbin to shortstop and Curtis Mead to third base. item.title: Bryson DeChambeau Backs LIV Reboot, Vows League Will Last Forever
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images As LIV Golf tries a major reboot, Bryson DeChambeau has signaled most strongly that he intends to return to the circuit. The two-time U.S. Open champion appeared on the “Figuring Out” podcast to discuss the league’s future following its Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing in September. While other stars have walked away, DeChambeau believes the new financial structure will finally work for the players and the organization. According to Central Oregon Daily , DeChambeau told host Raj Shamani that the league can now “make full financial sense.” He emphasized that the new model is being built to survive the long term. “The business model makes a lot of sense,” DeChambeau told host Raj Shamani. He added that the upcoming version of the tour will be handled correctly. “It’s no funny business, no nothing. It’s going to be done right. And this is going to be a league, hopefully, that exists forever.” Bankruptcy and Player Exodus The comments were made amid severe financial trouble. Money problems forced the league to end its 2026 season early, leading it to file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September. This financial collapse triggered a wave of departures. Tim Schmitt reported for Central Oregon Daily that at least 14 notable players have said they will not return to the new league. Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, and Sergio Garcia are among those who have opted out. Instead of joining LIV, Sergio Garcia, the 2017 Masters champion, plans to compete on the DP World Tour in 2027. According to Yahoo Sports , the roster of players committed to LIV Golf 2.0 remains short so far. Richard Bland, Cameron Tringale, Brendan Steele, Victor Perez, and Ben Campbell have publicly declared their commitment. Prior to the extended Oct. 30 commitment deadline, he had not made his plans public. Team Golf and Management Issues DeChambeau acknowledged that the original structure of the league had significant flaws. He expressed a strong desire to keep the team format but admitted the management failed to execute it well. “The point of it is that the team golf stuff, I was very excited about,” DeChambeau said. He explained that he still cares deeply about the team aspect of the game. “I really care, and I still do care deeply about the team golf stuff.” His criticism was directed at the upper leadership rather than the concept itself. “And the top company just wasn’t really managed that effectively. And I know that now … I didn’t know that during the time.” This admission suggests the new reboot aims to fix those specific management errors. item.title: Baltimore Ravens sign veteran quarterback after Lamar Jackson injury
item.description: Charles LeClaire-USA TODAY Sports The Baltimore Ravens’ quarterback room has been decimated by injuries over the past few days. Now, the team is bringing in some reinforcements. The Ravens are signing quarterback Kedon Slovis to their 53-man roster off the Green Bay Packers’ practice squad. He could be one of Baltimore’s options against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night. Ravens’ Quarterback Injuries Lamar Jackson suffered a right thumb injury on his first throw of Sunday’s 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills. He’s set to undergo surgery and is headed to injured reserve, and head coach Jesse Minter said the injury could “potentially” end his season. Backup Tyler Huntley then went down with a toe injury in the second quarter, forcing undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into his NFL debut. Fagnano went 10-of-21 for 91 yards with an interception. Fagnano is now dealing with an ankle injury of his own and was limited at Monday’s walkthrough, though Minter said he expects him “to have a chance to play on Thursday.” The Ravens also signed Austin Reed to their practice squad on Monday. Baltimore, which dropped to 4-4 with the loss, has reportedly shown interest in trading for a veteran quarterback as well. Kedon Slovis Joins the Ravens On Tuesday, the Ravens added another option at the position, signing Slovis off the Green Bay Packers practice squad. “A new QB in Baltimore: The Ravens are signing Kedon Slovis to their 53-man roster off the Packers’ practice squad, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports. The options for Thursday night against Jacksonville now include Joe Fagnano, Austin Reed and Slovis,” wrote Tom Pelissero . Slovis, 25, played college football at USC, Pitt, and BYU before making his NFL debut with the Arizona Cardinals last season. He appeared in two games and attempted just two passes. Ironically, his debut came against the Jaguars, when he replaced Jacoby Brissett after Brissett took a big hit from linebacker Devin Lloyd. He also has a connection to Baltimore’s coaching staff. Ravens quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork was Slovis’ position coach in Arizona last season. “Ravens QB coach Israel Woolfork was with Kedon Slovis in Arizona. Now, they’re back together in Baltimore,” Pelissero added . Needless to say, it’s been a chaotic week for the Ravens at quarterback, and it’s only Tuesday. item.description: Lee Westwood tied 14th in last week's Hong Kong Open on the Asian Tour [Getty Images] Lee Westwood says he has not signed for LIV 2.0 or held talks with the DP World Tour about a return, leaving the European Ryder Cup legend "unemployed" as he considers his future. The 53-year-old Englishman was among the high-profile players lured to LIV Golf when the controversial Saudi-backed breakaway tour began in 2022. LIV's future remains unclear after Saudi's Public Investment Fund (PIF) withdrew its backing - having pumped in more than $5bn (£3.8bn) - and led to the league filing for bankruptcy protection last month. It has secured a possible $300m (£224m) in financing from BC Partners Credit to try to move forward with LIV 2.0, but only a handful of players have so far committed to the proposed competition in 2027. In an interview with The Chipping Forecast podcast, Westwood said: "I'm currently unemployed. "There hasn't been anything presented to me that is agreeable for LIV 2.0, there are still a lot of things on that which need fine-tuning. I haven't signed for 2.0. I haven't signed anything." Westwood has been heavily criticised for pursuing the vast sums of money offered by LIV. The move cost him the chance to captain the European Ryder Cup team in 2023, but he says he would have "been stupid" not to set himself up financially for life. "I've made a fortune over the last four and a half years," added Westwood, who is reported to have won £16m in prize money on the LIV tour. "I don't really have to play golf again, but I still love playing golf so it's given [me] the option what to do over the next few years." Rahm unwilling to 'follow path' of LIV 2.0 Fellow European Ryder Cup player Jon Rahm says he decided to leave LIV because he "wasn't willing to follow the path" taken by the league as it fights for survival. It was the first time the 31-year-old Spaniard has spoken publicly since securing his exit from the series in October by reaching a separation agreement. Rahm was the reigning Masters champion when he was convinced to join LIV - a seismic move which underlined the scale of the league's ambition. "As much as I liked the project and the idea on, let's say, LIV 1.0, I wasn't thrilled with the changes they were doing to 2.0," Rahm said at the Abu Dhabi Championship, his first event since leaving LIV. "It wasn't anything special, anything that stood out. I just didn't like where they were going with 2.0." Rahm joined LIV in a deal worth a reported $300m (£222m), only to leave last month with $100m (£75m) - according to ESPN - owed on the remainder of the contract. "There were too many unknowns," added the two-time major winner. "It seemed like it was going a bit away from team golf. "It became more of a regular tournament. item.title: 24-year-old dies after collapsing during her first New York City Marathon
item.description: Rachel Apa, a first-time New York City Marathon runner in “perfect health,” died Sunday two miles short of the finish line . The 24-year-old Pennsylvanian, who played Division I field hockey at Bucknell University until 2023, texted “Ow ow” to her father Steve Apa when she was at mile 19, before collapsing at mile 24, according to The New York Times . Spectators ran to help Apa at around 1:30 p.m, including two doctors who administered CPR, before she was taken by ambulance to Mount Sinai Medical Center. Apa was declared dead at around 9:40 p.m, her father told The Times . He said his daughter had suffered a rare muscle condition brought on by exertion known as rhabdomyolysis . Rhabdomyolysis, also referred to as “rhabdo,” occurs when muscles break down and can poison the body. “It’s unfathomable,” Steve Apa said. “Perfect health, perfect shape, 24 years old.” Marathon deaths are rare with about 1 fatality in every 500,000 runners due to cardiac events, Emory School of Medicine research found. While dozens of runners have been treated for rhabdo during the NYC Marathon, according to a 2022 study, there appears to be no data on deaths during marathons from the condition. Rachel Apa, 24, was about to finish her first marathon when she collapsed Sunday afternoon at mile 24 (Bucknell Athletics) The Lewisberry native, who graduated magna cum laude in May 2024 with a bachelor’s degree in markets, innovation and design, worked as a product manager at TE Connectivity, an electrical component company. She had also begun an M.B.A program at Charleston Southern University and had been training for the marathon for months. She was fundraising for the Parkinson’s Foundation in honor of her grandfather, collecting $7,656.68, well over her $4,000 goal. “My grandfather was one of my role models growing up. He taught me to stay active, push my limits, and embrace challenges. After he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease, I watched as it slowly took away the freedom to move that he once loved,” she wrote on LinkedIn earlier this year. A spokesperson for the New York Road Runners, which organizes the marathon, said the non-profit was “deeply saddened” by the death. “Our thoughts and sincere sympathies are with the runner’s family, friends, and the entire running community,” the spokesperson told The Times . A spokesperson for Bucknell University told The Independent the school extends its deepest sympathy to Apa’s family and friends, noting that she was a “key contributor” to the school’s field hockey team who earned Academic All-Patriot League honors and scored 17 goals during her collegiate career. "The Bucknell community mourns her loss and extends its heartfelt condolences to all who knew and loved her," Mike Ferlazzo, the school's Director of Media Relations, said. item.description: Tottenham Hotspur v Crystal Palace FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Crystal Palace have appealed against the straight red card Jean-Philippe Mateta received in Saturday's 2-0 defeat at Tottenham. The France international faces a three-match ban for his studs-up challenge on Micky van de Ven, and losing him now would be a fresh blow for under-pressure Eagles boss Pierre Sage, with Liverpool visiting Selhurst Park on Sunday. Palace insist Mateta's challenge was accidental Palace have lodged an appeal against the red card shown to Mateta , who was sent off in the 13th minute at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The striker caught Van de Ven with his studs up as the pair contested a loose ball, and referee Michael Oliver initially showed him a yellow card. Oliver upgraded it to a red after being sent to the monitor by VAR Jarred Gillett. Palace believe the challenge was accidental, arguing that the Frenchman had his eyes on the ball and did not see Van de Ven coming. VAR says the challenge ticked every box for serious foul play Gillett left little room for doubt when advising Oliver on the incident. He said: "Point of contact is on the achilles, nowhere near the ball. He's sprinting at speed and with intensity, the studs catch him flush on the achilles. I think it ticks all the boxes for serious foul play." Oliver then explained the decision to the crowd over the tannoy: "After review, Crystal Palace No.14 makes full, forceful contact with the studs on his opponent's achilles. The final decision is red card." Sky Sports' Ref Watch panel of Dermot Gallagher, Tim Sherwood and Jay Boothroyd unanimously agreed on Monday that it was the right call. Mateta ban would leave Sage short of strikers Down to 10 men, Palace could not hold Spurs, and goals in either half from Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke sealed a comfortable win. The defeat left the Eagles in the relegation zone, with just one win from their last six Premier League matches. Losing Mateta would be another blow for Sage, who is fighting to save his job and had only recently welcomed the striker back from a hamstring injury. With Jorgen Strand Larsen out with an ankle problem, Eddie Nketiah would be Palace's only available forward. What next for Mateta and Palace? If the ban is upheld, Mateta will miss Sunday's home game against Liverpool before the international break, as well as crunch clashes with newly promoted Coventry and Hull. He would still be available when Palace host Hoffenheim and Real Sociedad in the Europa League.

item.description: Cody Gakpo breaks silence on failed Liverpool exit Cody Gakpo Stayed at Liverpool After £80m Manchester City Bid Fell Short Cody Gakpo came close to leaving Liverpool this summer. That much is clear. Tottenham Hotspur pushed early, Manchester City followed late, and for a while Liverpool were prepared to listen. Then the reality of the market kicked in. Tottenham were among the first to test the water in August, with Roberto De Zerbi looking to add another forward. Gakpo was on the radar, and Liverpool were not shutting the door. A few weeks later, Manchester City moved. Talks opened on August 29, and Gakpo was understood to be open to the Etihad if he was going anywhere. City then put real money on the table. Their offer was worth £80 million, made up of £75 million up front and another £5 million in add-ons. Liverpool said no on August 31. That is the key point here. They were not rejecting the player, they were rejecting the timing. Liverpool transfer decision came down to timing Liverpool’s concern was simple enough. Sell Gakpo that late in the window and replacing him properly becomes a gamble. Clubs know you are under pressure, prices go up, options narrow, and mistakes get made. Liverpool decided keeping a proven attacker was better than taking £80 million and scrambling for alternatives. Under Andoni Iraola, Gakpo has remained part of the plan. There has been no public drama and no attempt to reopen the issue. The player has addressed it directly ahead of the Champions League meeting with Fenerbahce, saying, “Not really, my mindset is the same. Try to perform. But it was quite a hectic summer regarding a lot of topics. I just try to enjoy football and enjoy life. It wasn’t much of a discussion was it? The decision was made and that’s it.” Cody Gakpo focus remains on Liverpool role That sounds like a player who understands the business and has moved on. Liverpool weighed up the fee, the squad picture and the market. In the end, they kept Cody Gakpo, and that was the sensible call.

item.title: Duce Robinson tears ACL, will miss rest of FSU football season
item.description: Florida State football star wide receiver Duce Robinson is out for the season after suffering a torn ACL in the Seminoles' 36-24 loss to Clemson on Saturday, Oct. 31 , first reported by ESPN and confirmed by the Tallahassee Democrat. Robinson did not play in the second half but remained on the sidelines. He didn't have his helmet with him and was walking gingerly as he supported his teammates. After posting 1,000 receiving yards in his debut campaign in Tallahassee, Robinson elected to return to school for his senior year and a second season with FSU, rather than pursue the NFL draft. In eight games this season Robinson posted 438 yards and four touchdowns on 24 receptions this season. When asked after the game, then-head coach Mike Norvell, who was fired Sunday, Nov. 1 , said he had no update on Robinson's prognosis. "I just knew that at halftime after he got checked out, we knew that he wouldn't be back in the game," Norvell said. FSU returns to the field on Saturday, Nov. 7 against Boston College . The program will be under the direction of interim head coach Rick Stockstill. Robinson's absence is another blow to an already wounded Seminoles offense, which lost star running back Ousmane Kromah to a season-ending ankle injury suffered against Miami. item.title: Giro d’Italia 2027 route revealed with iconic climbs set to appeal to 2024 champion Tadej Pogacar
item.description: The route of the 2027 Giro d’Italia has been unveiled, with the men’s race set to feature a trio of iconic climbs to attract the highest calibre of climber - although the likes of Jonas Vingegaard and Tadej Pogacar are expected to miss out. The Passo del Mortirolo, Passo Gavia and Monte Zoncolan will all feature in one edition of the race for the first time, with all three coming in a typically difficult final week. The race runs from Saturday 8 May to Sunday 30 May and begins in Trieste, briefly hopping over the border into Slovenia before returning to the north of Italy. The furthest south it reaches is Naples where there will be a sprint finish as usual, before a return to the Alps and Dolomites which will decide the champion of the 110th edition, ahead of the now-traditional processional final stage and sprint finish in Rome. The route, revealed in Rome on Tuesday, will traverse 3,418km and 50,250m of climbing over 21 stages, with two individual time trials, seven summit finishes and a mix of opportunities for the fast men and punchier, uphill finishes over the remaining days. The time trials total 56.9km and are split between a mountainous test to Campo di Giove and a flat, specialist-friendly route on the Monza motor racing circuit. The two tests against the clock are likely to appeal to Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe’s Remco Evenepoel and Decathlon CMA CGM’s Paul Seixas, major names the Giro will look to secure with defending champion Vingegaard widely expected not to return and 2024 winner Pogacar expected to target the Tour de France - Vuelta a Espana double instead of another tilt at the Italian grand tour, despite the parcours suiting the latter especially. The 2,600m Gavia returns for the first time since 2014 on a brutal queen stage on stage 16, the first day after the final rest day. The ascent - this year’s Cima Coppi, or highest point - is sandwiched between two climbs up the Mortirolo on the way to the line in Aprica. In total the Alpine test covers 192km and 5,700m of elevation gain and is highly likely to decide the destiny of the maglia rosa. Stage 16 of the Giro d'Italia 2027 (RCS) Stage 18 is another mountainous test with 4,450m of elevation gain on the cards but the general classification favourites may opt to keep their powder dry for the penultimate outing of this grand tour, with Monte Zoncolan returning on a stage which packs 3,600m of climbing into its last 50km. The route for the Giro d’Italia Women was also unveiled on Tuesday, with the race similarly tailor-made for the peloton’s best climbers including defending champion Demi Vollering of FDJ United-Suez. The 2027 edition covers 1,132km across the north-west of Italy and 17,450m of climbing, over 5,000m more than in this year’s race. As with the men’s race the maglia rosa will be decided in the Alps, first on a 11km mountainous time trial - similar to the Dolomites TT this year - and then on the final stage, the queen stage around Mont Blanc which takes in 4,000m of climb

item.title: England cricketer of the year named as star promises there is ‘plenty more to come’
item.description: Ollie Robinson is targeting further success in the second act of his Test career after being awarded the Bob Willis Trophy for England cricketer of the year. The seamer spent two-and-a-half years out of favour with the selectors before staging an impressive return this summer, taking 28 wickets at an average of just 9.32 against New Zealand and Pakistan. The 32-year-old is set for a key role in this winter’s red-ball programme, which includes tours to South Africa, Bangladesh and the 150th anniversary Test in Melbourne, before turning his attention to next summer’s home Ashes series. Despite making only four appearances this year - one against New Zealand followed by three against Pakistan - the weight of Robinson’s performance saw him recognised by members at the Vitality Cricket Media Club Awards at Lord’s, taking the trophy named after former England captain and fellow pace bowler Willis. Robinson came back into the fold after two-and-a-half years outside of the England setup (PA) "It’s a huge honour to receive this award. After spending such a long time away from the England side, to come back and have the summer I’ve had has been incredibly special," he said. "There were certainly some tough moments along the way, which makes receiving recognition like this mean even more. I’ve absolutely loved being back playing for England and hopefully there’s plenty more to come." Middlesex pace bowler Naavya Sharma, currently touring the West Indies with England Lions, collected the NV Play young cricketer of the year award following a breakthrough season. The award dates back to 1950, boasting a list of previous recipients that includes greats of the game such as Sir Geoffrey Boycott, Sir Ian Botham, Sir James Anderson, Joe Root and Ben Stokes. Teenage England spinner Tilly Corteen-Coleman, 19, won the Vitality Women’s young cricketer of the year prize after making debuts across both white-ball formats this summer. Kirstie Gordon picked up the JM Finn women’s cricket award after captaining The Blaze to a domestic treble, while Angus Brown was named England’s disability player of the year.
